findings.explanation: Splunkbase 5076 is 'Fix hostnames on UFs'. The Nutanix-built 'TA for Nutanix Prism' is Splunkbase 3103. The wrong ID also appears in references, implementation step 1 ('confirm 5076 is on a heavy tier'), and detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: Install the add-on as `Splunk_TA_nutanix` (TA for Nutanix Prism, [Splunkbase 5076](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/5076))
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 5076 with 3103 everywhere, and title the reference 'TA for Nutanix Prism (Splunkbase 3103)'.

findings.explanation: The Prism Element v2.0 /cluster object is not known to expose a numeric 0–100 cluster health score, and the listed aliases look guessed. GET /PrismGateway/services/rest/v2.0/cluster/services also does not appear in the v2.0 API; CVM service state usually comes from genesis status or cluster status.
findings.quote: fields such as `cluster_health_score` (alias on some builds: `health_score` / `healthScore` / `ClusterHealthScore`)
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Prism v2.0 API explorer and the TA for Nutanix Prism (3103) user guide for the actual health field and the service-status source. If none exists, describe a customer-built score.

findings.explanation: The sibling list puts Nutanix version compliance at UC-19.2.10 and protection-domain RPO at UC-19.2.31. UC-19.2.7 (CVM Health) already exists. The 19.1.x references, which also include the Prism Central alerts reference UC-19.1.26, point at the wrong subcategory.
findings.quote: AOS, NCC, and Foundation version drift is excluded here and is owned by UC-19.1.27 ... Snapshot, PD, and RPO policy posture is UC-19.1.28 ... CVM-only “node health” without cluster score is the future UC-19.2.7 lane
findings.suggested_fix: Point the exclusions at UC-19.2.10, UC-19.2.31, and UC-19.2.7 (existing), and confirm the right ID for Prism Central alerts.

findings.explanation: The SPL runs `where r>0` before the lookup and the rf_breach calculation. A cluster with a good score, no down services, and an RF breach is dropped, so an RF breach on its own never alerts.
findings.quote: A lower live `cluster_rf` than the governance `expected_rf` in the lookup is an automatic elevate-to-`high` in the SPL
findings.suggested_fix: Say that RF breach only raises rows that already alert, or have the SPL owner move the RF check before the r>0 filter.

findings.explanation: 'cassandra' here is the internal Nutanix metadata service, not an Apache Cassandra deployment, and m365, snmp, and snmp_ups have nothing to do with this UC. These tags will mis-route equipment filters.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep only nutanix in equipment, and nutanix_prism_element and nutanix_prism_central in equipmentModels.

findings.explanation: The search uses no data model, and a service UP/DOWN and health-score signal does not map cleanly to CIM Performance.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave cimModels empty, or justify the mapping with a cimSpl.

findings.explanation: Broken markdown bold markers appear in several places (here, in Step 4 KPIs, and in Step 5), and the long comment-macro digression is hard to follow. The text also ends with 'Anything less is a draft, not verified.', which is ironic next to status=verified.
findings.quote: and **cron */5 on the alert. The join uses a bounded window so a stuck CVM in NA** for longer
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the bold markers, cut the macro digression to one sentence, and remove the closing line.

findings.explanation: The text ends with a double period.
findings.quote: if the case is not an emergency..

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified, yet it cites the wrong Splunkbase app and field names that look guessed, so no SME verification is evident.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade the status until someone has checked the fields against a running TA for Nutanix Prism.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The final `sort 0 - severity_bucket, cluster` sorts strings in reverse alphabetical order (warning, info, high, critical), so critical rows land last, not first. Sort on sevord instead.
`where r>0` runs before the RF lookup, so rf_breach can never surface a row on its own. The second `where` that repeats `(r>0)` is redundant.

summary: The SPL combines a Prism cluster health score with critical CVM service state, and the implementation is detailed. But the add-on ID is wrong (5076 is not the Nutanix TA), the cross-references to sibling UCs point at the wrong subcategory, and the SPL's severity sort and redundancy-factor filter contradict the prose. The score field and the services endpoint look invented.
